[MUQATIL:9:75-79/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | When God granted the hypocrites bounty, they withheld it and turned away in refusal.
[TAB-FULL:v11p576/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Once God gave them wealth, they withheld charity, refused to maintain relatives, and did not spend for God; they turned away from their covenant. | mentions 9:75
[TAB-FULL:v11p576/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Their turning away and being averse refers to turning away from the covenant they had made with God. | mentions 9:75
[TAB-FULL:v11p576/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas identifies the man as the Anṣārī Thaʿlaba b. Ḥāṭib, who publicly pledged charity, giving each person their due, and maintaining kin; after receiving wealth he broke his promise, angered God, and his story was revealed in these verses.
[TAB-FULL:v11p579/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري | reports | Thalaba says he asked for wealth, promised to give every rightful person his due, and the Prophet prayed for him after his pledge.
[TAB-FULL:v11p579/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet warned Thalaba that a little wealth whose thanks he could render was better than much wealth he could not bear.
[TAB-FULL:v11p579/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري | reports | Thalaba's growing flock forced him out of Medina; he gradually left congregational prayers and eventually even Friday prayer, asking travelers for news.
[TAB-FULL:v11p579/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري | reports | After the verses about his broken pledge were revealed, Thalaba begged the Prophet to accept his charity, but the Prophet and then Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman refused; he died during Uthman's caliphate. | mentions 9:75, 9:77
[TAB-FULL:v11p581/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قتادة | reports | Qatada reports that an Ansari at an assembly vowed to give every rightful person his due if God granted wealth, but acted otherwise when wealth came.
[TAB-FULL:v11p581/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet recounted that Israelites asked Moses for a manageable set of commands instead of following the Torah while pursuing livelihoods; God gave them three commands, which they soon neglected.
[TAB-FULL:v11p581/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet promised Paradise to those who would not lie, break promises, or betray trusts and who guarded their eyes, hands, and private parts from betrayal, theft, and adultery.
[TAB-FULL:v11p581/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A report attributed to the Prophet says three traits mark a hypocrite even if he fasts, prays, and claims Islam: lying, betraying a trust, and breaking a promise.
[TAB-FULL:v11p581/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · آخرون | reports | Other authorities identify the two people behind the pledge as Thalaba and Mu'attib ibn Qushayr.
[TAB-FULL:v11p583/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan identifies the pledge-makers as Thalaba ibn Hatib and Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, both from Banu Amr ibn Awf.
[TAB-FULL:v11p583/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says two men left an assembled group after swearing that they would give charity if God granted them wealth, but withheld it when enriched.
[TAB-FULL:v11p583/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن زيد | reports | Ibn Zayd takes them as a class of hypocrites whose withholding caused hypocrisy to remain in their hearts until meeting God, without repentance, forgiveness, or pardon, as with Iblis.
[TAB-FULL:v11p583/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Al-Tabari says the verse makes broken promises and lying a sign of hypocrisy, an understanding also held by Companions and Successors and supported by reports from the Prophet. | mentions 9:75, 9:77
[TAB-FULL:v11p583/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عبد الله | reports | Abdullah says a hypocrite is recognized by lying, breaking promises, and treachery in a pact, and recites this passage as confirmation. | mentions 9:75, 9:77
[TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A report through al-Hasan attributes to the Prophet the saying that lying, betrayal of trust, and breaking a promise mark a hypocrite even if he prays, fasts, and claims Islam.
[TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · الحسن | reports | Asked whether promising repayment while temporarily unable to pay makes him a hypocrite, al-Hasan answers that this is how the hadith was transmitted.
[TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عبد الله بن عمرو | reports | Al-Hasan recounts that Abdullah ibn Amr's father fulfilled a promise to marry a man to his daughter on his deathbed so he would not meet God with a third of hypocrisy.
[TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عطاء بن أبي رباح | reports | Ata argues that Yusuf's brothers lied, broke a promise, and betrayed trust without being hypocrites, since their father and grandfather were prophets; this challenges treating the traits as universal proof of hypocrisy.
[TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · جابر بن عبد الله | reports | Jabir reports that the Prophet's three traits concerned hypocrites who lied to him, betrayed his confidential trust, and broke their pledge to campaign; a spy disclosed Abu Sufyan's location, occasioning 8:27 and 9:75–77. | mentions 8:27, 9:75, 9:77
[TAB-FULL:v11p586#2/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan agrees that Ata correctly traced the hadith's origin and that its three traits apply specifically to hypocrites.
[TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Al-Hasan transmits the Prophet's saying that lying, breaking promises, and betraying trusts make one a hypocrite, even if one prays, fasts, and claims Islam.
[TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عبد الله بن عمرو بن وائل | reports | On his deathbed, Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Wa'il said he had nearly promised a suitor his daughter and formally married her to him to avoid meeting God with a third of hypocrisy.
[TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قوم | reports | Some say the pledge-makers only intended their vow inwardly and never spoke it aloud.
[TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · معتمر بن سليمان التيمي | reports | Mu'tamir recounts forming an unspoken vow during a storm at sea; when he consulted his father Sulayman, his father told him to voice or fulfill it.
[TAB-FULL:v11p586#3/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · سعيد بن ثابت | reports | Said ibn Thabit says the vow was an inward intention not spoken aloud, citing God's knowledge of people's secrets and private conversations. | mentions 9:78
[TAB-FULL:v11p586/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عبد الله بن عمرو | reports | Abdullah ibn Amr says three traits make a person a hypocrite: lying when speaking, breaking promises, and betraying a trust; he recites this verse.
[TAB-FULL:v11p586/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · محمد بن كعب القرظي | reports | Muhammad ibn Ka'b says he eventually found hypocrisy's three signs—lying, breaking promises, and betrayal—in this passage and in the verse about the Trust offered to heaven and earth. | mentions 9:75, 9:77, 33:72

[THALABI:v5p72/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · النبي | reports | When Tha'laba later offered the charity, the Prophet said God had forbidden him to accept it and rebuked him for disobeying the instruction he had been given.
[THALABI:v5p72/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان | reports | After the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman each refused Tha'laba's repeated offers because the Prophet had rejected them; Tha'laba died during Uthman's caliphate.
[THALABI:v5p73/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · النبي | reports | A report from Ibn Umar through Masruq attributes to the Prophet four marks of complete hypocrisy and says any one persists as a mark until abandoned: lying, breaking promises, betraying covenants, and obscene conduct in dispute.
[THALABI:v5p73/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · النبي | reports | Al-Ash'ath transmits Hasan's report that lying, breaking promises, and betraying trusts make someone a hypocrite even if he fasts, prays, and claims belief.
[THALABI:v5p73/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · عبد الله بن مسعود | reports | Ibn Mas'ud lists lying, breaking promises, and betraying covenants as signs of hypocrisy and says God confirmed this in the passa

[QUSHAYRI:v1p434/r16] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Preferring anything over God’s pleasure is miserliness: a miser with wealth loses its blessing, one who withholds the self from obedience loses health, and one who withholds the spirit from God is forsaken until life becomes misery.
